readings.verb: shrink squares one ring, grow single cells to 9x9
readings.reading: Every solid square loses its outer ring (side n becomes n-2, placed one cell in from its top-left); a single cell instead grows into a 9x9 square (rows r-4..r+4, cols c-5..c+3). A 7x8 box became 5x5, so the new side is min(h,w)-2.
readings.why: every object in the output is the input object resized along the cycle 9->7->5->3->1->9; background elsewhere

readings.reading: Every solid square loses its outer ring (9x9->7x7, 5x5->3x3, 3x3->1x1) and every single cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on it, so square sizes cycle 1->9->7->5->3->1.
readings.why: each output object has the same colour and centre as an input object and side length cycled down by 2 (1 wraps to 9)

readings.verb: shrink squares one ring / grow dots to 9x9
readings.reading: Every solid square shrinks by one cell on each side (9x9->7x7, 5x5->3x3, 3x3->single cell), while a single cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on it; same colours, background 7.
readings.why: each output object is the input object's box inset by one, except 1x1 objects which become 9x9 centred

readings.reading: Each solid square is replaced, in place and concentrically, by the next size in the cycle 9->7->5->3->1->9: squares lose their outer ring, and a single cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on it.
readings.why: every output square has the input square's colour and centre and side (n-2), or 9 when n=1

readings.reading: Every solid square of side n is replaced by a concentric square of side n-2 in the same colour (a 3x3 becomes its centre cell); a single cell instead grows into a 9x9 square centred on it.
readings.why: every output object is a concentric square of the input square's colour with side n-2 (or 9 when n=1)

readings.verb: erase leftmost two columns of each object
readings.reading: The two leftmost columns of every object are erased to background; objects only two wide disappear.
readings.why: every cell in the first two columns of its object becomes 8 (the background); nothing else changes

readings.reading: Each object loses its two leftmost columns: those cells become background (objects 2 columns wide vanish).
readings.why: every changed cell lies in the leftmost two columns of its object and becomes the background colour 8; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Every object loses its two leftmost columns (relative to its own bounding box); objects only two columns wide vanish.
readings.why: output object = input object minus its two leftmost bbox columns

readings.reading: Every object loses the cells in the two leftmost columns of its bounding box (they become background); objects two columns wide vanish.
readings.why: exactly the object cells in the first two columns of each object's box turn to background colour 8; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Each object loses its two leftmost columns (those cells become background).
readings.why: every cell of an object within two columns of its leftmost column becomes background 8; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Two overlapping objects swap layering: in the overlap cells the colour of the object that was on top is replaced by the colour of the object that was underneath.
readings.why: only overlap cells change, and each takes the other object's colour

readings.reading: Two overlapping shapes swap their stacking order: in the overlap, the shape that was underneath is drawn on top, so the hidden shape becomes complete.
readings.why: only overlap cells change, and each becomes the colour of the shape whose bounding box/line is incomplete in the input

readings.reading: Two shapes overlap; the shape that was underneath is brought to the front, so the overlap cells take the hidden shape's colour.
readings.why: only cells where the occluded shape would continue change, and they become that shape's colour

readings.verb: swap layering (bring occluded shape to front)
readings.reading: Two overlapping shapes: the one that is partly hidden is brought to the front, so the overlap cells take the colour of the occluded shape and it is shown complete.
readings.why: after the change the previously occluded shape is a complete rectangle/line and the other shape loses exactly the overlap cells

readings.reading: Two single-colour shapes (rectangles or lines) overlap; the shape that was partly hidden is brought to the front, so the overlap cells take the hidden shape's colour.
readings.why: only overlap cells change, and each takes the colour of the shape that was occluded

readings.verb: frame each rectangle, width = dot count
readings.reading: Each yellow rectangle containing k dots of one colour gets a surrounding border of width k in that dot colour.
readings.why: around every rectangle the ring of thickness k (k = its dot count) is painted the dot colour; rectangle itself unchanged

readings.reading: Each colour-4 rectangle holding N dots of colour c gets a surrounding ring of colour c, N cells thick.
readings.why: around every rectangle the ring width equals its dot count and the ring colour equals the dot colour

readings.reading: Each yellow rectangle containing k dots of colour c gets a solid surrounding border of colour c, k cells thick.
readings.why: ring around each rectangle's box has thickness = dot count and dot colour

readings.reading: Each colour-4 rectangle contains N dots of some colour c; draw a border of colour c around the rectangle with thickness N.
readings.why: every rectangle is surrounded by a solid ring whose colour is its dot colour and whose width equals its dot count

readings.reading: Each colour-4 rectangle holds k single marks of one colour c; a solid ring of colour c and thickness k is drawn around the rectangle.
readings.why: around every rectangle the band of width k (k = mark count) is filled with the mark colour; the rectangle itself is unchanged

readings.reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.
readings.why: every background cell strictly between two diagonally aligned plus centres becomes 2; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background between them.
readings.why: every new colour-2 cell lies on a diagonal joining the centres of two pluses

readings.reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.
readings.why: every new 2 cell lies strictly between two diagonally aligned plus centres; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Plus-shaped objects whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 drawn on the background cells between them.
readings.why: every 2 cell lies on the diagonal between two plus centres that are diagonally aligned, and every such pair is joined

readings.reading: Plus-shaped objects whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.
readings.why: every background cell on the diagonal segment between two plus centres becomes 2; nothing else changes

readings.verb: lift each object by its height
readings.reading: Each bar standing on the bottom edge is lifted straight up by its own height.
readings.why: every object keeps shape and colour and its new top row = old top row minus its height

readings.reading: Every object moves straight up by a distance equal to its own height.
readings.why: each output object has the input object's shape and colour, shifted up by its height; old cells are cleared

readings.reading: Each object (resting on the bottom) is lifted straight up by a distance equal to its own height.
readings.why: each output object = input object shifted up by its bbox height, shape kept

readings.reading: Each bar standing on the bottom edge is lifted straight up by a distance equal to its own height.
readings.why: every object keeps its shape and column span and its rows shift up by its height

readings.reading: Each solid object moves straight up by a distance equal to its own height.
readings.why: every object keeps shape and colour and its box shifts up by exactly its height

readings.reading: The whole 3x3 grid is painted with the input's most frequent colour.
readings.why: every output cell equals the mode colour of the input

readings.reading: The whole 3x3 grid is filled with its most frequent colour.
readings.why: every output cell equals the input's most frequent colour

readings.reading: The whole grid is filled with the most frequent colour of the input.
readings.why: output is uniform in the input's majority colour

readings.reading: The whole grid is filled with its most common colour.
readings.why: the output is uniform and its colour is the input's majority colour

readings.reading: The whole grid is painted with its most common colour.
readings.why: every non-majority cell takes the majority (background) colour

readings.verb: push attached pieces away from the core to the edge
readings.reading: Each 9-coloured core stays put; every other object touching a core is pushed away from it in the direction of the side it touches, until it reaches the grid edge.
readings.why: every moved object keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side opposite the core; pieces already at the border stay

readings.reading: A colour-9 skeleton stays fixed; every other coloured piece attached to it slides straight away from the 9 it touches until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.
readings.why: each non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border in the direction pointing away from the adjacent 9; 9 cells never move

readings.reading: Colour-9 pieces stay fixed; every other piece attached to a 9 slides straight away from that 9 until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.
readings.why: each non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side facing away from its 9 neighbour

readings.verb: push pieces away from hub to border
readings.reading: Small pieces attached to a colour-9 hub slide away from the hub, in the direction they stick out from it, until they reach the grid border; the 9 hub stays.
readings.why: each piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side it pointed to; hub unchanged

readings.verb: push pieces away from hub to border
readings.reading: A hub of colour 9 stays fixed; each other-coloured piece attached to it slides straight away from the 9 cell it touches until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.
readings.why: every non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side facing away from the adjacent 9 cell

readings.verb: slide to wall and cap with 8 line
readings.reading: The green shape slides toward the red wall until it touches it, then a full line of 8 is drawn just beyond the shape on the side away from the wall.
readings.why: the shape keeps its form and ends in contact with the 2 line; the row/column adjacent to the shape on the far side becomes all 8

readings.verb: push to wall and back with line
readings.reading: The colour-3 shape is pushed against the full colour-2 wall line, and a full line of colour 8 is drawn parallel to the wall right behind the shape on the far side.
readings.why: the 3 shape keeps its shape and touches the 2 wall; one full 8 line sits immediately behind it

readings.verb: slide to bar and back with 8 bar
readings.reading: The green shape slides toward the red bar until it touches it, and a full bar of 8 is drawn right behind the shape on the side away from the red bar.
readings.why: shape keeps its form and touches the 2 line; one 8 line parallel to it touches the shape's opposite side

readings.verb: slide to wall and mark the back
readings.reading: The 3-shape slides toward the 2-line until it touches it, and a full line of colour 8 is drawn alongside the 3-shape's box on the side away from the 2-line.
readings.why: the 3-shape keeps its shape and touches the 2-line; the 8 line is directly behind it

readings.reading: The colour-3 shape moves straight toward the full colour-2 line until it touches it, then a full line of colour 8 is drawn on the shape's far side, parallel to the 2 line.
readings.why: the 3 shape keeps its shape and ends in contact with the 2 line; the full line adjacent to its opposite side is 8

readings.reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner behind 8 borders; every dot in the square field is recoloured with the key colour of the field quadrant it lies in.
readings.why: each dot's new colour is the key entry matching its quadrant of the field; key, 8 border and background unchanged

readings.reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner; the dots of the dotted square field are recoloured by quadrant: dots in each quadrant of the field take the key colour in the same position of the key.
readings.why: each dot's new colour equals the key cell in the same quadrant position; non-dot cells are unchanged

readings.reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner; each dot in the main area is recoloured with the key colour of the quadrant of the area it lies in.
readings.why: each dot cell takes the colour of the key cell for its quadrant; nothing else changes

readings.reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner beyond the 8 bars; the square work area is split into four quadrants and each dot takes the key colour at the matching quadrant position.
readings.why: every dot's new colour equals the key cell whose position matches the dot's quadrant

readings.reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner beside a square field of one-colour cells; the field is split into four quadrants and every coloured cell takes the key colour of its quadrant.
readings.why: every field cell of the mark colour becomes the key colour at the same relative quadrant; nothing else changes
